description: A three-species food chain: grass feeds bunnies and bunnies feed foxes, and one knob takes the chase from a steady rest through period doubling into chaos.

params.text: Sets the speed the simulation runs at, -8 to +4 octaves; the centre gives C4 at 261.63Hz at the periodic default and the bottom about 1Hz.
Sets the saturation of the bunny-to-fox link, 0 to 1, mapped onto a narrow band around 2, which reshapes the chase and moves the chaotic windows.
Sets the bifurcation parameter, 0 to 1, taking the chain from rest through a regular chase and period doubling into chaos at about 0.62, and on into deep crashes.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the upper trophic saturation.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the bifurcation parameter.

inputs.text: Adds to the RATE knob at 1V per octave, setting the speed the simulation runs at.
Modulates the upper trophic saturation, at a tenth per volt through its attenuverter.
Modulates the bifurcation parameter, at a tenth per volt through its attenuverter.
A continuous force added to the grass at a quarter unit per volt, clamped to ±15V first: a short gate re-times the ecology and an audio-rate signal cross-modulates it.

outputs.text: The grass population centred on its equilibrium, at a gain of 8 and soft-clipped to ±5V.
The bunny population centred on its equilibrium, at a gain of 18 and soft-clipped to ±5V.
The fox population centred on its equilibrium, at a gain of 2.5 and soft-clipped to ±5V.
A 10V pulse 1ms long at each local maximum of the grass population.
A 10V pulse 1ms long at each local maximum of the bunny population.
A 10V pulse 1ms long at each local maximum of the fox population.

notes: The peak outputs are events, not a three-phase clock. At the periodic default they tick once each per lap in grass, bunny, fox order; in chaos the order and the count vary.
The three populations are not equally spaced in phase, and the output gains of 8, 18 and 2.5 exist to bring their very different native swings to a comparable level.
